catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from Continuous Architecture System (CAS) CLI Runner and repository governance knowledge bases, focusing on subagent declarations, pipeline execution, LLM abstractions, and agent telemetry.
analysis_limits: Repository inspected via AST metadata, directory tree, and key file interfaces
Dynamic multi-turn agent evaluation traces inspected via schema and runtime configurations

system_map.overview: ideas-to-life-cas provides a Continuous Architecture System (CAS) orchestrating autonomous and human-in-the-loop software architecture tasks. It standardizes subagent skill packages, executes sequential workflow steps via FlowRunner, tracks multi-provider coding agent telemetry, and enforces compliance guardrails over agent-generated architecture artifacts.

agents.name: verifier
agents.role: Evaluates architectural deliverables and rules compliance prior to state transition

agents.name: agentic-merger
agents.role: Reconciles, synthesizes, and merges distributed knowledge updates and architecture decision records

orchestration.description: Centralized pipeline orchestration via FlowRunner coordinates step sequencing and compliance gates, while individual subagents execute discrete specialized skills declared in markdown manifests and invoke LLMs through a unified client.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLM Gateway
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access across heterogeneous LLM providers with retry, fallback, and mock support.

tools_and_integrations.name: Agent Telemetry Adapter
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Normalizes OpenTelemetry spans, token usage, and cost estimates from coding agents like Claude Code and Antigravity.

state_and_memory.description: File-backed architecture knowledge graph, execution profiles, rules, and decision records organized under cas-knowledge/.
Computed governance health, throughput, compliance findings, and token cost rollups calculated from spans and artifacts.

patterns.name: Declarative Subagent and Skill Manifests

tool_protocols.notes: Skills define modular directory bundles containing operational scripts and agent contracts.

optimisation_targets.notes: Decouples agent personas and discrete competencies from Python execution logic.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Subagents are given scoped instructions while boundary limits are maintained by directory structure.

patterns.summary: Capsule-like skill and subagent definitions encapsulated as isolated markdown declarations and scripts for portability across Claude and general agents.
patterns.intent: Standardize agent capabilities into composable, discoverable packages that work across multiple agent runtimes.
patterns.context: Agent definitions in .agents/ and .claude/ folders containing distinct directories for skills such as cas-audit-agent-rules, cas-drawio-generator, and subagents like verifier.
forces: Vendor lock-in across agent harnesses (e.g., Claude Code vs IDE agents)
Prompt divergence when agent skills are embedded in executable application code
patterns.solution: Define capabilities as modular Markdown contracts and executable skills in standard root folders (.agents/skills and .claude/skills), mirrored to agent runtime configs.
implementation_signals: Dedicated skill folders with task-specific scripts under .agents/skills/
Role descriptions encapsulated in markdown files (e.g. verifier.md)

evidence.note: Declares verification subagent role and responsibilities.
Mounts and links skill definitions into agent workspace configurations.

benefits: Allows agent skills to be audited and versioned independently of runner code
Ensures interoperability between developer tools and automated runners
costs: Risk of schema drift between .agents/ and .claude/ definitions if not synchronized by bootstrap
failure_modes: Skills defined in markdown falling out of sync with underlying script arguments

patterns.reuse_notes: Package agent roles and tools as standard filesystem directory trees so agents can inspect them via filesystem discovery.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline Context Propagation

tool_protocols.notes: Steps accept structured input context and return updated context dictionaries.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures deterministic step-by-step verification and flow control.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Execution follows explicit steps configured in flow plans rather than unconstrained self-prompting.

patterns.summary: Coordinates multi-step agent and analysis tasks through an explicit FlowRunner passing shared context between stages.
patterns.intent: Maintain deterministic boundaries and predictable execution order across multi-phase agent tasks.
patterns.context: Executing automated architecture analysis, validations, and sync actions in src/cas_runner/runner.py.
forces: Unpredictability of fully autonomous multi-step agent loops
Need for reproducible step-level telemetry and status reporting
patterns.solution: FlowRunner coordinates sequential phases, propagating a shared mutable or cumulative context and capturing results at each milestone.
implementation_signals: Passing context dictionary or model across execution phases

benefits: Clear failure boundaries and step isolation
Easy integration with telemetry and health checks
costs: Less flexibility than fully dynamic adaptive replanning
failure_modes: A failure in an early step blocking subsequent independent validations

patterns.reuse_notes: Use FlowRunner-style orchestrators when tasks require sequential compliance steps before committing external mutations.

patterns.name: Heterogeneous Agent Telemetry Normalization

tool_protocols.notes: Parses diverse trace logs from external coding agent harnesses into common metrics.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables uniform cost tracking and health assessment across divergent agent CLI runs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standardizes agent telemetry without constraining internal agent autonomy.

patterns.summary: Adapts heterogeneous agent execution logs and spans into a normalized OpenTelemetry-compatible span model with dollar-cost estimations.
patterns.intent: Track agent activities, compute dollar costs, and monitor duration across different coding agent providers uniformly.
patterns.context: Agent telemetry parsing in src/cas_runner/dashboard/agent_telemetry.py supporting Claude Code, Antigravity, and generic coding agents.
forces: Diverse trace formats generated by Claude Code, open-source agents, and vendor harnesses
Need to track aggregate spending and health across distributed runs
patterns.solution: Define a unified AgentTelemetrySpan dataclass/model, and implement targeted adapter classes (ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter) with pricing calculation heuristics.
implementation_signals: Provider-specific telemetry adapters subclassing or implementing parse protocols
Normalized AgentTelemetrySpan containing provider, token counts, and cost estimation

evidence.note: Defines data contract for agent telemetry and provides concrete adapters for Claude Code and Antigravity.

benefits: Accurate cost tracking across mixed AI developer environments
Decouples dashboard health calculations from provider-specific log schemas
costs: Adapter maintenance required as external agent CLI log formats evolve
failure_modes: Inaccurate cost calculation if provider pricing tables fall out of date

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement adapters parsing session JSON logs into normalized spans whenever supporting multiple agent toolchains.

patterns.name: Model Gateway Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Centralizes model invocations via LiteLLM client with mock fallback.

optimisation_targets.notes: Allows swapping models and using mock clients for deterministic local testing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Isolates LLM invocation complexity behind a single client interface.

patterns.summary: Abstracts foundation model access behind a LiteLLM client interface paired with a mock implementation for unit testing and offline execution.
patterns.intent: Decouple agentic components from specific model vendors while enabling offline, zero-token test fixtures.
patterns.context: LLM client module in src/cas_runner/llm/ used by governance and merging engines.
forces: Vendor API shifts and rate limits during automated tests
Requirement to test agent reconciliation logic without invoking paid LLM endpoints
patterns.solution: Wrap LiteLLM calls into LiteLLMClient and mirror its interface with MockLLMClient that returns predefined structured responses.
implementation_signals: MockLLMClient companion class returning deterministic synthetic outputs

evidence.note: Encapsulates model call dispatching, timeout handling, and parameter normalization.
Provides deterministic responses for test suites without network egress.

benefits: Zero CI token costs during test runs using mock client
Seamless model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, and local providers
costs: Mock client may not exhibit subtle model hallucinations seen in production
failure_modes: Provider configuration mismatch when switching between local mock and live endpoints

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt LiteLLM with a symmetrical mock client to test agent loops in hermetic CI pipelines.

patterns.name: Finite State Governance Transition Engine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions evaluate transition legality before changing architecture status.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees agent proposals cannot skip mandatory review or compliance verification stages.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Strict state machine controls prevent rogue agent modifications.

patterns.summary: Enforces formal transition rules and validation checks before agent actions or knowledge updates can transition lifecycle states.
patterns.intent: Prevent agents or automated scripts from performing illegal state jumps on architectural decisions and governance items.
patterns.context: Governance action management in src/cas_runner/governance/governance_action_engine.py and governance_action_service.py.
forces: Uncontrolled agent drift resulting in draft decisions being marked as approved without peer review
Auditability requirements for changes in enterprise architecture repositories
patterns.solution: Register permissible state transitions in a TransitionRegistry and gate all state updates through GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry maintaining valid from_state -> to_state edges
GovernanceActionEngine validating transition preconditions and recording resolution events

evidence.note: Implements transition verification and execution for governance actions.
Provides service interface to execute valid state machine operations.

benefits: Guaranteed consistency of artifact status across multi-agent workflows
Clean audit trails recorded in ResolutionResult objects
costs: Requires upfront mapping of all valid transition graphs
failure_modes: Agents blocked from resolving unexpected edge cases if transitions are too rigidly defined

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a transition registry to constrain agent mutations on persistent records, requiring pre-checks before state changes.

patterns.name: Agentic Knowledge Reconciliation and Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Uses LLM synthesis to reconcile conflicting knowledge documents into unified records.

optimisation_targets.notes: Reduces manual burden of resolving distributed architectural knowledge conflicts.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automates text synthesis while adhering to strict governance models.

patterns.summary: Uses an LLM-assisted reconciliation agent to resolve semantic conflicts and merge distributed knowledge updates into canonical architecture records.
patterns.intent: Synthesize differing architecture drafts, project changes, and governance signals into a unified canonical knowledge base.
forces: Parallel teams or agents proposing overlapping changes to architecture documents
Standard git merge conflicts in prose documentation resulting in fragmented semantic records
patterns.solution: Feed both source and target documents along with resolution context into AgenticMerger, using structured prompting to reconcile discrepancies.
implementation_signals: AgenticMerger class orchestrating LLM prompt synthesis for merging documents
Resolution models returning reconciled content and diff summaries

evidence.note: Orchestrates semantic merging of governance and architecture records.

benefits: Preserves rationale and nuances from both source updates without human merge tedium
Enforces common Markdown template structure during reconciliation
costs: Requires secondary validation to confirm agent did not hallucinate compromise facts
failure_modes: Accidental loss of critical architectural constraints during automated synthesis

patterns.reuse_notes: Combine semantic LLM mergers with deterministic pre- and post-validation checks before saving changes back to git.

patterns.name: Compliance Guardrail Engine

tool_protocols.notes: Evaluates domain rules against workspace state and produces compliance metrics.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unauthorized drift by verifying agent modifications against formal rule contexts.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automated guardrail overrides agent discretion when rule violations are detected.

patterns.summary: Audits proposed code and architecture modifications against formal compliance rules, outputting structured findings and risk assessments.
patterns.intent: Detect violations of architectural principles, unapproved dependency additions, and governance anomalies before workflows complete.
forces: Agents generating technically valid code that violates organizational architectural standards
Need for programmatic pass/fail signals to gate CI/CD workflows
patterns.solution: Execute ComplianceEngine against workspace artifacts to generate ComplianceFinding lists and GovernanceRisks summaries before allowing promotions.
implementation_signals: ComplianceEngine checking rule-context against target repositories
Generation of structured ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics models

evidence.note: Evaluates architectural constraints against files and traces.
Data models capturing findings and health metrics.

benefits: Immediate feedback loop alerting agents or developers to architectural regressions
Quantitative compliance scoring for repository health dashboards
costs: Rules must be continually curated in rule-context.json to prevent false positives
failure_modes: Silent pass if rule definition syntax contains undetected omissions

patterns.reuse_notes: Run automated compliance evaluation after each agent action stage before triggering git commits or PR creations.

patterns.name: Workspace Steering Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Injects governance rules, Claude settings, and workspace symlinks into the developer agent environment.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures coding agents working in the workspace inherit architecture rules automatically.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Guides agent context without requiring manual prompt crafting by developers.

patterns.summary: Projects enterprise governance rules, subagent skills, and settings into the local workspace and IDE configuration files during bootstrapping.
patterns.intent: Guarantee that interactive agent sessions (like Claude Code or IDE copilots) operate with current architecture rules without manual copy-pasting.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/bootstrap.py updating .claude/settings.json and AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md files.
forces: Agent prompt context drift when rules are updated in central repos but not in local developer projects
Friction for developers setting up new repositories with agent skills
patterns.solution: Provide a bootstrap command that merges governance blocks into project instruction files and symlinks or copies required skills into .agents/ and .claude/ directories.

evidence.note: Projections of settings and skills into target workspace paths.

benefits: Zero-effort synchronization of rules to AI assistants working in developer repos
Centralized rule changes automatically propagate into agent prompts
costs: Risk of overwriting custom user settings if merge logic is too aggressive
failure_modes: Broken symlinks if target paths are moved or mounted across incompatible containers

patterns.reuse_notes: Use structured markdown markers (e.g. CAS:START / CAS:END) to non-destructively project agent steering context into developer documentation.

anti_patterns.name: Untracked Agent Cost Leakage
symptoms: Autonomous agents running iterative bash/refactoring loops without recording token expenditures or model parameters
Unexpected cloud billing spikes from uncontrolled prompt retries

where_observed.note: System introduced explicit fallback cost estimators because external agent harnesses frequently emit partial token data.

impact: Inability to calculate ROI for automated developer agents and danger of cost overruns.
suggested_remediation: Enforce mandatory span telemetry emission for all agent tasks and configure budget thresholds in execution profiles.

anti_patterns.name: Unvalidated Knowledge Mutation
symptoms: Agents committing updates directly to architecture decisions or governance maps without triggering verification subagents or compliance checks
Invalid state transitions appearing in governance dashboards

where_observed.note: Engine specifically exists to prevent unconstrained direct edits by enforcing allowed transitions.

impact: Corrupted architecture repository state and erosion of human trust in autonomous agent contributions.
suggested_remediation: Require all knowledge mutations to pass through TransitionRegistry checks and verifier subagent approval prior to merge.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Standardizing telemetry across multiple coding agent CLI tools (Claude Code, Antigravity) into OpenTelemetry-compatible traces and calculating dollar cost rollups.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enables uniform observability into agent performance, speed, and cost regardless of which underlying agent generated the work.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Validating transitions against a formal TransitionRegistry and running static ComplianceEngine checks before actions are applied.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Separates agent proposal capabilities from approval and commit capabilities.

open_questions.question: How are real-time tool calling permissions and human approval escalations handled when the AgenticMerger encounters mutually incompatible architectural decisions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If reconciliation fails or detects contradictory principles, the agent needs a deterministic escalation mechanism rather than defaulting to an arbitrary compromise.
open_questions.evidence_gap: The AgenticMerger symbol is defined in governance/agentic_merger.py, but specific interactive human-in-the-loop escalation hooks in CLI mode were not fully traceable from top-level imports.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine src/cas_runner/governance/agentic_merger.py implementation details and specs for interactive escalation prompts.
